subject: Discovery recap & PoC plan — ShopSmart integration
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Nguyen <lisa.nguyen@shopsmart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & PoC plan — ShopSmart integration

Hi Lisa —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed PoC/onboarding plan so we’re aligned. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain points you called out:
- Customer support cost from QA/returns due to poor intent detection across chat + email.
- Latency and cost spikes in peak hours for your existing hosted model (3rd-party API).
- Difficulty integrating generative features into your Node-based checkout microservice (lack of good SDK samples and rate-limiting behavior).

Current stack (as discussed):
- Backend: Node (Express) for checkout microservice; Python (internal data team) for offline processing.
- Hosting: AWS (us-east-1) with RDS/Postgres, Redis for caching.
- Current model endpoint: third-party hosted API (pay-as-you-go), limits on token throughput.

Success criteria for a successful PoC (we agreed):
1) Latency: 95th percentile < 250ms for typical chat generation workload at test load.
2) Cost: <= 60% of current per-token spend at comparable quality.
3) Integration: working SDK-based integration into the Node checkout service and a simple Python batch for offline eval.
4) Quality: equal-or-better intent detection / reranking vs current baseline (via provided test prompts).

Proposed PoC scope & timeline (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): access & security onboarding (SOC2 checklist + API keys) — owners: Lisa (ShopSmart) + Priya (Redwood Security)
- Week 1: SDK integration into Node checkout + sample calls to dev endpoint (owner: Marissa)
- Week 2: Load testing and latency/cost profiling with your synthetic traffic (owner: Ben)
- Week 3: Quality evaluation vs baseline; tune batching/quantization suggestions (owner: Marissa)
- Week 4: Final report, roll / next steps for Dedicated or Hosted (owner: Ben)

Integration details we need from you to start:
- Preferred SDK language(s): Node (primary), Python (secondary) — please confirm.
- API compatibility: you mentioned using OpenAI-compatible endpoints for some infra — confirm if you require strict OpenAI API compatibility (we can provide an adapter) or are ok using Redwood-native SDKs.
- Security evidence: SOC2 report, data retention expectations, and whether you need private deployment (VPC) for the PoC.

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft technical requirements worksheet (shop-smart-technical-requirements.xlsx) for you to fill with endpoints, sample payloads, and traffic patterns.

Next steps / meeting:
- Can we schedule a 30-min tech kickoff the week of Apr 5? Suggested times: Tue Apr 6 10–11am PT or Wed Apr 7 2–3pm PT.
- Action owners to confirm: please reply with SDK preference + who from your side will be the technical owner (Tom? someone else).

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachment: shop-smart-technical-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Lisa Nguyen <lisa.nguyen@shopsmart.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@shopsmart.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & PoC plan — ShopSmart integration

Thanks Ben — great summary and aligned on the success criteria. A few clarifications from our side: 

- SDK preference: Node is primary for the checkout microservice. Our data science team (Python) will want example Notebook snippets but they aren’t owning the integration.
- API compatibility: We prefer something OpenAI-compatible to minimize changes to our orchestration layer, but we can consider a Redwood-native SDK if you provide a small compatibility adapter.
- Security: I’m attaching our initial security questions (ShopSmart_Security_Qs.pdf). We are SOC2 compliant but will need to confirm how API keys and access are logged. Priya, can you confirm the logging/audit guidance?

Technical owner: Tom Alvarez (cc’d) will be the technical lead from ShopSmart. He’ll join the kickoff.

Availability for kickoff: Tue Apr 6 10–11am PT works for us.

Thanks,
Lisa
Director, Product — ShopSmart Retail
lisa.nguyen@shopsmart.com

Thanks Lisa — great. Confirming: Tue Apr 6 10–11am PT for the kickoff — I’ll send a calendar invite shortly.

Quick answers / next items from Redwood: 
- We can provide an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and also a Redwood-native SDK for Node + Python. Our recommended path for fastest integration is: Node SDK -> use our adapter for any OpenAI-specific orchestration. We’ll include small sample snippets in the kickoff.
- Security/audit: Priya will follow up with our SOC2 summary and explain API key rotation and audit logs. Priya — can you send the SOC2 excerpt and a short note on log retention (recommended default) by EOD Tue?

Attached: Draft PoC plan (PoC-plan-v1.pdf) with milestone owners and test cases.

Action items (Ben): create calendar invite, set up dev API keys, provide sample Node snippet before kickoff.
(Action owners: Ben / Marissa / Priya / Tom)

Best,
Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & PoC plan — ShopSmart integration

Hi all — looping in from the solutions side. I’ll own the integration work and will prepare:
- Node SDK quickstart (5–10 minute sample you can drop into checkout)
- A simple Python notebook for the data team to run offline quality tests
- A small test harness for load profiling (to simulate peak checkout traffic)

Notes:
- For the PoC we recommend starting with our medium-latency profile and enabling KV/prefix caching for checkout prompts — that typically hits your latency goals while reducing token cost.
- If you need strict OpenAI API parity, we’ll include an adapter in the repo; otherwise our Node SDK is simpler and smaller to integrate.

I’ll share the quickstart and test harness before the kickoff (EOD Mon Apr 5 PT).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Lisa Nguyen <lisa.nguyen@shopsmart.com>

Perfect — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirmed:
- Kickoff Tue Apr 6 10–11am PT with Tom as technical lead.
- SDK preference: Node for integration; Python snippets for offline evaluation.
- Security: Tom and I will review Priya’s follow-up and the SOC2 excerpt once available.

We’ll fill out the technical requirements worksheet and return it ahead of the kickoff. Looking forward to the PoC.

Cheers,
Lisa
